What we lend against

The art we lend against

We lend against works with an established market — artists with an auction record, editioned prints, and sculpture. Provenance and condition shape the valuation, and a single work or a whole collection can be pledged.

Paintings

Oil, acrylic and watercolour by artists with an established auction record.

Editioned prints

Signed and numbered editions, valued on artist, edition size and condition.

Sculpture and objects

Bronze, marble and mixed media, including editioned casts.

Collections

A single advance against several works, rather than piece by piece.

What it costs to borrow

Priced below the high street, in writing

Your work is researched against auction records for that artist — the medium, the period, the edition and the condition — rather than valued on impression. That means an accurate valuation and a competitive loan, at rates lower than the typical high-street pawnbroker.

£500 upwards

How it works

Four steps. Back on your wall at the end.

Step 01

Tell us about your work

Send the artist, what you know of the work’s history, and a few photos. A specialist researches it and sends an indicative offer the same day.

Step 02

Send it to us, insured

Specialist fine-art transport, arranged and fully insured — or bring smaller works to our City of London office by appointment.

Step 03

Accept the offer and get paid

Once we have examined the work in person we confirm the valuation. Accept, and the money is with you within 24 hours.

Step 04

Back on your wall at the end

Loans run for six months and can be extended. Repay early and you pay less, with no penalty. Your work is returned exactly as it arrived.

How we value fine art

Researched against the auction record

Every work is researched against what that artist actually achieves at auction — for that medium, that period and that size — and assessed for condition and provenance. We do not value art on impression.

Attribution checked

Signature, medium and period examined, and questioned where they should be.

Valued against auction records

Comparable results for that artist, not a generic estimate.

Provenance weighed in

Receipts, catalogues and exhibition history lift the valuation.

Nothing sight-unseen

You see the valuation before you commit to anything.

Why Trinity rather than the high street

A pawnbroker for art you intend to keep.

A dealer or auction house sells your work, and it is gone — often months later, after fees. We don’t. A pawn loan is a loan — you keep ownership, we keep it safe, and you take it back when you repay.
